$comment: Neutral shipped <intrin.h> (Microsoft compiler-intrinsic header) — c113. sqlite3.c's `#if defined(_MSC_VER) ... #if !defined(SQLITE_DISABLE_INTRINSIC)` block (~line 15130) does `#include <intrin.h>` + `#pragma intrinsic(...)`; DSS resolves the include here, so the build proceeds WITHOUT -DSQLITE_DISABLE_INTRINSIC. ★ TWO CLAIMS THAT USED TO SIT HERE WERE FALSE AND ARE CORRECTED. (1) 'DSS drops the pragma (unknown directive, C 6.10.6p2)' stopped being true at TF-C82, which replaced the silent drop with the `preprocess.pragmaEffects` REGISTRY -- and because no row claimed `intrinsic`, this exact pragma then BROKE the pe64 leg (MEASURED: 448 of 2135 error[P0020]). TF-C85 gave it a row (`realizationRequestOnly`): the pragma asks HOW a listed name is realized, never WHETHER it exists, and DSS picks realization itself, so ignoring it is safe FOR A STATED REASON rather than by silence. (2) 'so the amalgamation compiles' named the wrong artifact: the corpus builds are USE_AMALGAMATION=0, i.e. 189 separate TUs, and the reaching sites are `src/sqliteInt.h:312-315` (x 112 TUs) -- not `sqlite3.c`. The amalgamation carries the same block because it is generated from those sources; the harness does not build it. availableObjectFormats:[pe] — an MSVC compiler-intrinsic header is meaningless on elf/macho (a reference there fails loud, mirroring windows.json/process.json). The intrinsics themselves are NOT symbols here: `__umulh`, `_ReadWriteBarrier` AND the three `_byteswap_*` are pure compiler intrinsics with NO library export, realized as always-on lowered BUILTINS in c-subset.lang.json (`lowering:umulh`/`lowering:barrier`/`lowering:bswap`) — declaring a non-export in `symbols` eager-imports it and breaks the pe loader with STATUS_ENTRYPOINT_NOT_FOUND (0xC0000139), EMPIRICALLY re-confirmed: msvcrt.dll exports NO _byteswap_* (objdump -p, positive control memcpy/_msize/puts) and a draft that declared them crashed the loader exactly so. THE RULE SURVIVES THE FIX — do not 'simplify' the bswap builtins into a `symbols` row. ~~ A CLAIM THAT SAT HERE WAS FALSE AND IS RETRACTED: this comment used to say the `_byteswap_*` family was unreferenced because 'sqlite's byte-reverse fast path is #if'd out under DSS's config (SQLITE_BYTEORDER!=1234)'. **SQLITE_BYTEORDER IS 1234 under DSS**, MEASURED: x86_64.target.json:12 defines `__x86_64__` UNGATED, which is one of the arms of sqliteInt.h:996-1002. What actually chose the MSVC spelling is the OTHER half of each `#elif` chain — `_MSC_VER`=1943 clears sqlite's `MSVC_VERSION>=1300`, while GCC_VERSION=4002001 (from __GNUC__=4/__GNUC_MINOR__=2/__GNUC_PATCHLEVEL__=1) MISSES sqlite's `>=4003000` and `>=4008000` gates, so every `__builtin_bswap*` arm is dead and the chain falls through to `_byteswap_*`. Only pe64 errored because only pe defines `_MSC_VER`; elf/macho fall through once more to the portable byte-by-byte `#else`. MEASURED before the fix: exactly 3 `error[S0001] got _byteswap_*` on the pe64 testfixture (btreeInt.h:743 x1, util.c:1856+1869 x2) — the testfixture never linked, so the entire Windows unit corpus could not run. D-CSUBSET-INTRINSIC-BSWAP (a dedicated bswap builtin lowering: x86 BSWAP 0F C8+rd / arm64 REV16-REV-REV(X), chosen by a PER-WIDTH capability probe over the config-declared opcode vocabulary, with a universal-ALU byte-reversal fallback for a width no target encodes — x86 has no width-16 BSWAP) closed it 2026-07-31. Non-empty content = the honest `size_t` typedef: MSVC's real <intrin.h> makes size_t visible (its prototypes use it, via the vcruntime include chain); u64 = the pe64/LLP64 x64 width (string.json/stdio.json convention).
